mcqs.question: Who was identified as the Chief Minister of Assam after the 2026 Assembly elections?
mcqs.explanation: Himanta Biswa Sarma was identified as the Chief Minister of Assam. V.D. Satheesan, Suvendu Adhikari and N. Rangasamy were associated with Kerala, West Bengal and Puducherry respectively.

mcqs.question: Who was identified as the Chief Minister of Kerala after the 2026 Assembly elections?
mcqs.explanation: V.D. Satheesan was identified as the Chief Minister of Kerala. C. Joseph Vijay, Himanta Biswa Sarma and Suvendu Adhikari were associated with Tamil Nadu, Assam and West Bengal respectively.

mcqs.question: Who was identified as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu after the 2026 Assembly elections?
mcqs.explanation: C. Joseph Vijay was identified as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. N. Rangasamy, Suvendu Adhikari and V.D. Satheesan were associated with Puducherry, West Bengal and Kerala respectively.

mcqs.question: Who was identified as the Chief Minister of West Bengal after the 2026 Assembly elections?
mcqs.explanation: Suvendu Adhikari was identified as the Chief Minister of West Bengal. Himanta Biswa Sarma, C. Joseph Vijay and N. Rangasamy were associated with Assam, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry respectively.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Rajendra Arlekar was named as the Governor of both Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
Statement B: R.N. Ravi was named as the Governor of both Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: Rajendra Arlekar was named as the Governor of both Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Statement B is false because R.N. Ravi was listed as the Governor of West Bengal, not both Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly identifies the State/UT with the most seats and the State/UT with the fewest seats among the five Assembly-election jurisdictions?
mcqs.explanation: West Bengal had the most seats, with 294, while Puducherry had the fewest, with 30. Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Assam do not form the stated most-to-fewest pair.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the new poll measures announced for the 2026 Assembly elections, consider the following statements:
1. The measures were announced by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
2. EVMs would carry colour photographs of all candidates.
3. A polling station could have a maximum of 1,200 voters.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The measures were announced by CEC Gyanesh Kumar, included colour photographs of all candidates on EVMs, and set the polling-station cap at 1,200 voters.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding election-related information:

List-I
(a) Voter Information Slip
(b) Election Commission of India
(c) Establishment of the Election Commission of India
(d) Headquarters of the Election Commission of India

List-II
(i) New Delhi
(ii) Clear polling station details
(iii) Constitutional body
(iv) 25 January 1950
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iii, c-iv and d-i. The Voter Information Slip provides clear polling station details; the Election Commission of India is a constitutional body, established on 25 January 1950, with its headquarters in New Delhi.

mcqs.question: Which set of elections is conducted by the Election Commission of India?
options: Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice President
Only the offices of President and Vice President
State Legislatures and local bodies only
mcqs.explanation: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice President. The narrower alternatives omit parts of this stated mandate, while local bodies are not included in it.
